title: Satchin Panda Resigns From Salk Institute After Sexual Misconduct Allegations
excerpt: Indian-origin circadian biology researcher leaves prestigious California institute after 22 years following workplace misconduct investigation
body:
• Indian-origin biologist Satchidananda "Satchin" Panda will leave the Salk Institute on August 13 after 22 years, following a workplace misconduct investigation triggered by a female research assistant's complaint.
  • The journal Science reported that Salk had previously investigated Panda over separate allegations and taken disciplinary action, raising concerns about institutional transparency.
  • Panda's circadian rhythm and time-restricted eating research brought millions of dollars to the institute and influenced global health guidelines on meal timing.
  • The resignation echoes a 2018 case at Salk when cancer biologist Inder Verma stepped down after eight women accused him of sexual harassment.

Satchidananda "Satchin" Panda, one of the world's most recognized circadian biology researchers, will resign from the Salk Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California, on August 13, ending a 22-year tenure at the prestigious research centre. The departure follows an independent investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct filed by a female research assistant in his laboratory.

The Salk Institute confirmed in a statement that a staff research assistant raised concerns about workplace misconduct through official channels in March 2026. "The Institute offered support and resources to the staff member and initiated a prompt, thorough, and impartial investigation," the statement said. The woman, whose identity has not been disclosed, later left the institute voluntarily.

Panda Denies Allegations

Panda denied the allegations in an email to the journal Science. "I am deeply committed to maintaining a safe, respectful, and professional environment for everyone in my research team and across the Institute. These values are central to my leadership," he wrote.

However, Science reported a more troubling detail: according to a source with knowledge of the matter, Salk had previously investigated Panda over separate allegations of sexual misconduct and had taken disciplinary action. Some current and former employees told the journal they were concerned that allowing Panda to resign without publicly disclosing the investigation's findings could let him move to another institution without colleagues being aware of prior concerns about his conduct.

A Career Defined by Circadian Science

Panda, who was born in India's Odisha state, built his reputation on groundbreaking research into circadian rhythms — the molecular mechanisms underlying the body's internal 24-hour clock. His laboratory's work on time-restricted eating demonstrated that limiting food consumption to a consistent 8-to-12-hour window prevented obesity and improved glucose regulation in animal models. Follow-up clinical trials showed that eating within a 10-hour window improved weight, blood pressure, and glycemic control in patients with metabolic syndrome.

His research contributed to public health guidelines on reducing night-time blue-light exposure and fuelled the global popularity of intermittent fasting as a lifestyle intervention. The work brought millions of dollars in funding to the Salk Institute.

Pattern of Misconduct Allegations at Salk

Panda's departure is the second high-profile resignation from the Salk Institute tied to sexual misconduct allegations. In 2018, cancer biologist Inder Verma stepped down after eight women — six of them affiliated with the institute — accused him of harassment spanning four decades. Verma denied the allegations. The institute also faced gender discrimination lawsuits from three senior female scientists who alleged Salk was an "old boys club" that systematically obstructed their career advancement.

"Some current and former employees were concerned that allowing Panda to resign without publicly disclosing the investigation could allow him to move to another institution without colleagues being aware."

— Science journal report, July 2026

Impact on the Indian Scientific Community

Panda's case adds to a growing list of Indian-origin scientists at elite Western institutions facing scrutiny over workplace conduct. For the Indian diaspora in academic research — a community that has long celebrated figures like Panda as proof of Indian scientific excellence abroad — the allegations raise uncomfortable questions about accountability and institutional culture in top-tier laboratories.

The Salk Institute declined to share further details of the confidential personnel matter, including the investigation's findings or its outcome. Panda's formal departure date is set for August 13, 2026.
